question: Should OpenClaw core accept `includeFamily` as the model/client-facing reset-family history contract, including bounded archive visibility and rejecting `includeFamily` with `offset`?
rationale: The implementation is reviewable and proven, but it changes the public Gateway/tool protocol and session-history visibility semantics; automation cannot choose that permanent product/API contract for maintainers.

options.title: Accept the `includeFamily` contract
options.body: Approve the opt-in selector, bounded reset-family archive visibility, and offset rejection, then proceed with normal exact-head merge checks.

options.title: Narrow or redesign the API
options.body: Keep the PR open while maintainers decide whether this should instead be folded into a broader archive/logical-history API.

options.title: Decline core API expansion
options.body: Close the PR as not accepted product direction and ask for a smaller proposal or plugin/tool-level alternative.

recommendation.title: Accept the `includeFamily` contract
recommendation.body: Approve the opt-in selector, bounded reset-family archive visibility, and offset rejection, then proceed with normal exact-head merge checks.
